---
title: "Multiple criteria"
---

The same units can rank differently across criteria. A common report assigns one grade per unit and evaluates those grades on every criterion. A domain profile gives each domain its own column.

## Common grades {#common-grades}

The same grade column states a direction on every criterion. [Two scores](two-scores.qmd) shows what happens
when those directions conflict. [Criterion-specific costs](common-grade-cost.qmd) compares each criterion's risk
under the shared grades with its own minimum. [Withheld comparisons](why-withheld.qmd) traces why individual
directions are left unranked.

{{< include _apps.md >}}

## Domain profiles {#domain-profiles}

Separate columns allow two units to rank in opposite directions on different domains. The five examples
examine which domains can be graded separately, how a joint error limit changes that choice, and what the
resulting profiles look like for forty fictional sites. See the [Domain profiles guide](../profiles/index.qmd).
